---
title: "Module 2 — Working with LLM APIs and Open-Weight Models"
subtitle: "Day 1, hours 4–5 · theory, then the lab"
---

Module 1 drew the boundary. This module fills it with competence: the chat/messages
contract deeply enough to debug it, token accounting you can budget with, the error
taxonomy as designed behaviour, and an open-weight model served behind the exact
same interface.

By the end, "which model?" stops being a brand preference and becomes an
engineering comparison with numbers attached.

# Theory

## 1. Two wire dialects

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    subgraph OA["OpenAI chat completions"]
      direction TB
      O1["messages: [{role, content}]<br/>system is just the first message"]
      O2["max_tokens optional"]
      O3["content is a string"]
      O4["finish_reason: stop | length |<br/>tool_calls | content_filter"]
    end
    subgraph AN["Anthropic Messages"]
      direction TB
      A1["system is a TOP-LEVEL parameter"]
      A2["max_tokens REQUIRED"]
      A3["content is a list of typed blocks<br/>text · tool_use · tool_result"]
      A4["stop_reason: end_turn | max_tokens |<br/>tool_use | refusal"]
    end
    OA --> N["**Normalised**<br/>LLMRequest / LLMResponse"]
    AN --> N
    style N fill:#eef3fb,stroke:#4a76b8,stroke-width:3px
```

An adapter that pretends the differences do not exist produces subtle bugs. That
is precisely why Module 1's normalised types exist — and the differences are not
static:

::: {.callout-warning}
## A fifth difference, found while building this course

As of `anthropic` 1.x the Messages API **no longer accepts `temperature` or
`top_p` at all** — sampling moved behind `output_config.effort`, and structured
outputs moved to `output_config.format`. Forwarding `request.temperature` raises a
`TypeError`, which is how this was found rather than read.

The normalised `LLMRequest` keeps `temperature`, because the OpenAI dialect still
has it. The adapter is where the divergence stops, and
[`anthropic_client.py`](https://github.com/MohammadYusif/llm-application-engineering/blob/main/murshid/src/murshid/llm/anthropic_client.py)
says so in a comment that tells the next person not to "fix" it.

This is the module's real lesson in miniature: **APIs drift underneath your
lesson.** Trust an executed run over what should work from reading the docs.
:::

### Read the response as carefully as the request

`finish_reason` is control flow, not metadata:

| Value | What it means | What the application must do |
|---|---|---|
| `stop` | the model finished | proceed |
| `length` | **silently truncated** at `max_tokens` | treat as an error class, or raise the budget deliberately — never ship the fragment |
| `tool_calls` | the conversation is *not over* | run the tool loop (Module 3) |
| `refusal` | a content filter fired | designed UX, not a stack trace |

`usage` is the raw material of Module 6. Every adapter surfaces it, always —
including on streamed responses, where losing it is the classic cost-accounting
bug.

## 2. Sampling, determinism, and tokens

**Sampling.** `temperature` scales the logits: 0 for extraction and anything
validated downstream, 0.2–0.5 as a task default, 0.7+ for creative variance.
Adjust temperature **or** `top_p`, not both — tuning both is folklore, not
engineering.

::: {.callout-important}
## Temperature 0 does not mean reproducible

Fixed seed and temperature 0 still do not guarantee bit-identical output across
snapshots, hardware, or batch composition — GPU non-associativity and server-side
batching see to that.

Determinism in LLM systems comes from **validation and evaluation** (Modules 3 and
5), never from sampling settings. Tests that assert exact strings on generative
output are the flaky-test factory of this field.
:::

**Tokens.** Models bill, budget and think in tokens. And here the course's own
handout was wrong, so we measured:

```bash
make token-report      # 100 parallel Arabic/English sentence pairs
```

| Encoding | English | Arabic | ar/en | chars per token (en / ar) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cl100k_base` — GPT-4 / GPT-3.5 era | 1022 | 2373 | [2.32×]{.measured} | 5.05 / 1.38 |
| `o200k_base` — GPT-4o era onward | 1022 | 1005 | [0.98×]{.measured} | 5.05 / 3.26 |

The "Arabic costs 1.5–2.5× more" figure that has been in course material for years
is a fact about a *tokenizer generation*, not about Arabic — and it largely
vanished between two vocabularies. The rule underneath it survives and is the one
worth teaching:

> **Count with the route's own tokenizer.** `tiktoken` for OpenAI-dialect models,
> the provider's count-tokens endpoint for Anthropic, the model's own Hugging Face
> tokenizer for open weights. Three different answers for the same string, all
> correct for their model.

`murshid.llm.tokens` maps model ids to encodings for exactly this reason. Counting
an open-weight model's context with `tiktoken` under- or over-budgets by tens of
percent, and the symptom is intermittent context-length errors *below* your
computed budget.

## 3. Streaming, rate limits, and the error taxonomy

**Streaming** is server-sent events: deltas, closed by a final frame carrying
`finish_reason` and — if you asked for it — `usage`.

```python
stream_options={"include_usage": True}   # or usage never arrives
```

Accumulate deltas; surface time-to-first-token and total separately; **make sure
the last chunk's usage reaches the cost meter.** Streaming also changes the failure
model: an error mid-stream arrives after the user has seen half an answer, so
`ResilientClient` deliberately refuses to fail over once a token has been emitted —
splicing two models' answers together is worse than an honest error.

**Rate limits** are multi-dimensional (requests/minute *and* tokens/minute, per
model, per key tier). A 429 is normal operation at scale, not an outage: honour
`Retry-After`, back off with jitter, and shape load upstream.

| Status | Class | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | malformed request — a *bug* | never retry |
| 401 / 403 | credentials, permissions | page a human |
| 404 | model name typo | config bug |
| 413 / `context_length_exceeded` | budget violation | your forecast was wrong |
| 429 | rate limit | back off, honour `Retry-After`, cap attempts |
| 500 / 502 / 503 / 529 | provider side | retry, then fail over |
| timeout | either | retry once, then fail over |

Run it:

```bash
make drill-429      # 429s with Retry-After: 2 on the primary model, three minutes
make ask Q="كيف أجدد رخصتي التجارية؟"
make drill-off
```

You will see `llm_retry` honouring the header, then `fallback_served` from the
on-premise route, and a citizen who got an answer.

## 4. Serving open-weight models with vLLM

Two ideas make self-hosting economically real, and both are worth teaching
properly:

- **PagedAttention** manages the KV cache — the per-sequence attention state that
  dominates GPU memory during serving — in fixed-size pages rather than contiguous
  allocations. No fragmentation, many more concurrent sequences per GPU.
- **Continuous batching** admits and retires sequences from the running batch at
  every generation step instead of waiting for the whole batch. This is *the*
  economic argument for self-hosting.

Sizing, roughly: weights ≈ parameters × bytes/parameter (a 7B model ≈ 14 GB at
bf16, ≈ 4–5 GB at 4-bit), plus KV-cache headroom governed by
`--gpu-memory-utilization`, with `--max-model-len` bounding per-sequence KV cost.

```bash
# infra/vllm/serve.sh — one command turns a checkpoint into an OpenAI-compatible API
vllm serve ALLaM-AI/ALLaM-7B-Instruct-preview \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --served-model-name murshid-onprem --api-key "${VLLM_CLASS_KEY}"
```

The payoff is the config entry, not the command:

```yaml
routes:
  vllm:
    base_url: "http://gpu-server.classroom.local:8000/v1"
    residency: on_premise
    aliases: { murshid-default: murshid-onprem }
```

`OpenAICompatClient` works unchanged. That one line is Module 1's boundary
argument, proven.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Benchmark at realistic concurrency

Benchmarking vLLM at concurrency 1 and concluding self-hosting is slow is the most
common mistake in this section. Continuous batching's benefits appear *under load*.
Twenty-four participants hitting the class GPU at once is not a problem to fix — it
is the demonstration.
:::

## 5. Commercial versus open-weight, decided like an engineer

| Criterion | Commercial API | Self-hosted open weights |
|---|---|---|
| Frontier quality | strongest available | gap narrows yearly; task-dependent |
| Arabic quality | strong on flagships — verify per task | Arabic-centric models competitive on many tasks — **measure** |
| Data residency / PDPL | depends on provider region and DPA | full control; data never leaves your network |
| Cost shape | per token, zero idle cost, scales to zero | per GPU-hour; cheap **only** above a utilisation break-even |
| Ops burden | none — their pagers ring | yours: GPUs, drivers, upgrades, capacity, on-call |
| Customisation | prompting, provider fine-tunes | full: LoRA, logit control, tokenizer access |
| Snapshot control | provider deprecates on their schedule | you pin forever |

Four teaching points:

1. **The answer is usually a portfolio, not either/or.** Murshid routes general
   traffic to a commercial API and residency-classified traffic to vLLM, through
   one boundary.
2. **The break-even is computable** — and it has two answers, not one.
   `make breakeven` compares against *both* hosted tiers: a single-GPU 7B never
   beats a small hosted model on price, and beats the flagship tier above roughly
   25% sustained utilisation.
3. **Quality claims are settled by your golden set**, never by a leaderboard.
4. **Capability constraints are part of the matrix.** In this course's own
   measurements the open-weight route loses most on the `service` slice — tool
   contracts, not prose — which is exactly what shapes the routing table.

Measured on this repository ([`BENCHMARKS.md`](https://github.com/MohammadYusif/llm-application-engineering/blob/main/murshid/BENCHMARKS.md)):

| Backend | Overall | ar | safety | service | Cost per suite |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flagship | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 65.0 halalas |
| small | 95% | 95% | 100% | 83% | 2.7 halalas |
| open-weight | 94% | 92% | 100% | 75% | 26.0 halalas |

## 6. Common mistakes

1. **Retrying 400s.** Three times the bug, three times the cost.
2. **Losing `usage` on streamed responses.** Cost dashboards undercount the
   majority of traffic and nobody notices until finance does.
3. **Tuning temperature *and* `top_p`**, then attributing the change to a prompt
   edit.
4. **Assuming temperature 0 is reproducible**, then asserting exact strings.
5. **Benchmarking vLLM at concurrency 1.**
6. **Tokenizer mismatch** — counting an open-weight model's tokens with `tiktoken`.
7. **English-only evaluation of an Arabic-serving product.** This is the failure
   mode the course's bilingual corpora exist to prevent.

# Lab — Two providers, one interface

*Day 1, hour 5 · 50 minutes · pairs*

::: {.session-meta}
Objective
: Run the one contract suite against every adapter, serve the open-weight route
  with no code change, measure time-to-first-token, survive a live 429 storm, and
  record the first provider-comparison table.

Setup
: Module 1's lab complete. Gateway running.

You finish with
: Contract tests green on every adapter, a fault-drill log excerpt, and a
  `BENCHMARKS.md` seeded with real numbers.
:::

### 1 · The Anthropic adapter (12 min)

Read `AnthropicClient.complete()`. Four differences from the OpenAI dialect are
load-bearing, and the adapter is where each one stops:

| Difference | If you get it wrong |
|---|---|
| `system` is a **top-level parameter** | the system prompt is silently ignored |
| `max_tokens` is **required** | `400 max_tokens: field required` |
| content is a list of typed **blocks** | tool calls vanish |
| the finish signal is `stop_reason` | your `finish_reason` control flow never fires |

::: {.callout-warning}
### And a fifth, which the docs will not warn you about

As of `anthropic` 1.x, `messages.create()` **does not accept `temperature`** —
sampling moved behind `output_config`. Forwarding it raises a `TypeError`.

Do not delete `temperature` from `LLMRequest` to make the error go away: the
OpenAI dialect still has it, and the whole point of the normalised type is that
each adapter absorbs its own dialect's quirks. The comment in
`anthropic_client.py` tells the next person the same thing.

APIs drift underneath a lesson. Trust an executed run over what should work.
:::

Then run the contract suite — **the same test class, against every adapter**:

```bash
pytest tests/llm/test_adapter_contract.py -v
```

```
test_adapter_contract.py::TestAdapterContract::test_satisfies_the_protocol[fake] PASSED
test_adapter_contract.py::TestAdapterContract::test_satisfies_the_protocol[openai_compat] PASSED
test_adapter_contract.py::TestAdapterContract::test_satisfies_the_protocol[anthropic] PASSED
test_adapter_contract.py::TestAdapterContract::test_satisfies_the_protocol[vllm] PASSED
...
16 passed
```

"Implements the protocol" is a test, not a docstring claim.

### 2 · The open-weight route, with no code change (8 min)

The route already exists in `configs/murshid.yaml`. Read it, then use it:

```bash
make ask ROUTE=vllm Q="ما هي خطوات إصدار سجل تجاري؟"
```

```
[faq → murshid-onprem via vllm] 431ms, 1674 in (0 cached) / 187 out, 0.304 halalas
بخصوص إصدار سجل تجاري جديد لمؤسسة فردية: ...
```

Note the `model_id`: `murshid-onprem`. **Nothing in `src/` changed.** In the
classroom the same route points at `vllm serve` on the GPU box:

```yaml
routes:
  vllm:
    base_url: "http://gpu-server.classroom.local:8000/v1"
    residency: on_premise
```

That single config entry is Module 1's boundary argument, and this is the moment
it stops being an argument.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
### On the real GPU box, watch `nvidia-smi` on the projector

Twenty-four participants hitting one vLLM instance is not a problem to fix. It is
continuous batching, and it is the best explanation of the idea you will ever give.
:::

### 3 · Streaming and time-to-first-token (12 min)

Run the streaming path. `stream_options={"include_usage": True}` is what keeps
usage on the final frame.

```bash
make stream Q="What documents do I need to renew my commercial registration?"
```

```
About Renewing a commercial registration (CR): ...

[TTFT 593ms · total 707ms · 1406 in (0 cached) / 138 out]
```

Record **both** numbers in `BENCHMARKS.md`. Then answer, in one sentence: does
streaming reduce total latency?

It does not. It reduces *perceived* latency. Generation time is unchanged — which
is why Module 6 treats TTFT and generation as two separate levers with two
different fixes.

::: {.callout-important}
### The bug this task exists to prevent

Without `include_usage`, `usage` never arrives and the cost meter silently
undercounts the majority of traffic. The contract test asserts the final frame
carries it:

```python
assert final.usage is not None, (
    "losing usage on the final frame is the classic streaming "
    "cost-accounting bug — the meter silently undercounts most traffic"
)
```
:::

### 4 · The fault drill (10 min)

The instructor fires this without warning. You can also fire it yourself.

```bash
make drill-429       # 429s with Retry-After: 2 on the primary model, three minutes
make ask Q="كيف أجدد رخصتي التجارية؟"
```

Watch the log:

```
[warning] llm_retry  hop=primary attempt=1 status=429 retry_after=2.0 delay_s=2.0
[warning] llm_retry  hop=primary attempt=2 status=429 retry_after=2.0 delay_s=2.0
[warning] fallback_served  hop=fallback:vllm model_id=murshid-onprem
```

Then:

```bash
make drill-off
make stats           # faults_served, and what the gateway saw
```

Paste the log excerpt into your lab worksheet. Three things to notice:

1. the retry **honoured the header** rather than guessing a backoff;
2. attempts were **capped** — retries multiply cost and tail latency;
3. the citizen got an answer, from the on-premise route, and never knew.

A pair whose Module 1 lab skipped the `ResilientClient` wiring crashes publicly here. That
is the lesson; handle it kindly.

Try the harder one too:

```bash
make drill-outage    # the primary model returns 529 for five minutes
```

Then look at the token report and revise whatever you believed about Arabic:

| Encoding | en | ar | ar/en |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cl100k_base` | 1022 | 2373 | 2.32× |
| `o200k_base` | 1022 | 1005 | 0.98× |

The "Arabic costs about twice as much" rule of thumb is a fact about a tokenizer
generation. On a current vocabulary it is gone. The rule that survives is the one
underneath: count with the route's own tokenizer.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `400 max_tokens: field required` | the adapter forwarded `None` | `max_tokens` is required in the Messages API — the lesson, live |
| System prompt ignored on the Anthropic route | sent as a message inside `messages` | split it to the top-level `system` parameter |
| `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'temperature'` | the anthropic 1.x change | do not forward it; the comment in the adapter explains why |
| `usage` is `None` on streamed calls | missing `stream_options` | add `{"include_usage": True}` and check the final frame |
| The drill does nothing | a fault targets one model | `make stats` — check `fault` and `faults_served` |
| vLLM route slow for everyone at once | 24 participants at concurrency 24 | expected. Discuss continuous batching; do not "fix" it |

### If you finish early

Compute the estimate for the Module 6 kickoff. Murshid handles 30,000
conversations a day, averaging six turns, roughly 900 input and 150 output tokens
per turn. What does routing 70% of turns to the cheap model save per month at the
course price sheet's rates?

Check your arithmetic against `make replay-after` on Day 3 — and notice, when you
do, that your estimate was probably conservative in one direction and wildly
optimistic in another.
